info.bio:
El grupo Boston se crea a mediados de 1969 por el ingeniero del MIT Tom Scholz como guitarrista y principal compositor, además del vocalista Brad Delp, el guitarrista Barry Goudreau y el baterista Jim Masdea. Tras un inicio algo incierto, en el cual presentaron varios demos, el baterista Jim Masdea deja el grupo y es reemplazado por Sib Hashian, además de que el bajista Fran Sheehan se incorpora a las filas del grupo. Es así, como en 1976 y gracias a las composiciones ingeniosas del Scholz, el grupo lanza en 1976 su primer álbum titulado simplemente "Boston" y colocando inmediatamente éxtios en las listas de popularidad con la clásica "More than a feeling" y con "Peace of mind". El trabajo de Scholz se puede ver, asimismo, en la enigmática "Hitch a ride", una de las piezas más completas del disco. La voz de Delp es, además, un total acierto y se nota cierta innovación en el sonido del grupo a comparación de otras bandas de la época.

Para 1978, el grupo lanza su segundo álbum titulado "Don´t look back", el cual es de notable menor calidad que su antecesor y no deja muy satisfecho a Scholz, que acusa a la discográfica de haberlo presionado para emitir este material. A pesar de esto el disco alcanza ventas que le llevan al disco de platino y la canción que da título al álbum se convierte en un éxito comercial. Posteriormente comienza un litigio legal entre la discográfica y el grupo que durará años y que obligará a esperar durante ocho años para escuchar el siguiente álbum de Boston. El guitarrista Gary Phil sustituye a Guodreau y Fran Sheehan deja también al grupo. Scholz financia sus grabaciones vendiendo equipo, debido al asunto entre CBS y Boston. En 1982 el baterista Sib Hashian deja al grupo.

En 1986 se lanza, por fin, "Third stage" y la canción "Amanda" llega inmediatamente a las listas de popularidad. Este tema consta de un sonido muy distinto a las anteriores: una balada muy de los años ochenta acertada por Scholz y la gran voz de Delp. El álbum alcanza disco de platino. Delp deja Boston en 1990 y es sustituido por Fran Cosmo.

El siguiente álbum de Boston aparece hasta 1994, titulado "Walk On" y que retoma ciertos sonidos de hard rock de los inicios del grupo. Los arreglos de la canción que titula al disco (dividida en tres segmentos) son considerados excesivos por algunos, pero la canción es una de las mejores piezas compuestas y arregladas por el ingenioso Scholz. Delp regresa al grupo en 1994.

El siguiente trabajo del grupo es "Corporate America" lanzado en 2002, ya con algunas tendencias pop y otras buenas canciones. Es curioso que participen Fran Cosmo y su hijo Anthony, además de que entra Kimberley Dahme en el bajo y en la voz algunas veces. Jeff Neal (batería) completa una alineación extensa en este álbum.

Fran Cosmo y su hijo dejaron al grupo a principios de 2006 para formar su propia banda, dejando en ese momento a Brad Delp como única voz del grupo. Se especuló sobre una posible reunión con Barry Goudreau durante este periodo.

Una de las aportaciones de Tom Scholz es la tecnología "Rockman", que fue utilizada por Def Leppard en su álbum "Hysteria".

El 9 de marzo de 2007 una de las mejores voces en la historia del rock, Brad Delp, falleció en New Hampshire, EE.UU., a los 55 años de edad.

info.wikipedia:
Boston es una banda estadounidense de hard rock y rock progresivo formada en los años setenta y liderada por el músico virtuoso Tom Scholz.

El grupo Boston se crea a mediados de 1969 por el ingeniero del MIT Tom Scholz como guitarrista y principal compositor, además del vocalista Brad Delp, el guitarrista Barry Goudreau y el baterista Jim Masdea. Tras unos inicios algo inciertos, en el cual grabaron varias demos, realizadas en el estudio de Tom Scholz ubicado en el sótano doméstico de este; luego el baterista Jim Masdea deja el grupo y es reemplazado por Sib Hashian, mientras que el bajista Fran Sheehan se incorpora a las filas del grupo, que hasta el momento funcionaba como una banda a medio camino entre el circuito de aficionados y el profesionalismo de tiempo completo en los bares y pubs del circuito costero de bandas de rock de la ciudad de Boston. De hecho tanto Bradley Delp como Tom Scholz, tenían trabajos estables de tiempo completo fuera de la escena musical, durante esta primera etapa de la banda los miembros de la primera formación del grupo se habían conocido indistintamente interactuando y compartiendo papeles musicales en otras bandas locales. En los años previos a la edición de su primer LP, las demos realizadas fueron enviadas a varias compañías discográficas, como muestra para una eventual grabación y edición, y frecuentemente se recibía la respuesta (a confesión del propio Tom Scholz) "...esta banda no tiene nada que ofrecer...".

Fue así como, en 1976, y gracias a las composiciones ingeniosas de Scholz, el grupo publica ese mismo año su primer álbum titulado simplemente "Boston", tomando como base las demos realizadas en el estudio particular de Tom Scholz, que fueron remasterizadas y remezcladas en los afamados estudios "The Record Plant" en California, saltando de inmediato a los primeros puestos de las listas de éxitos con el clásico "More Than a Feeling" y con "Peace of Mind". El trabajo de Scholz se puede ver, asimismo, en la enigmática "Hitch a Ride", una de las piezas más completas del disco. La voz de Delp es, además, un total acierto y se nota cierta innovación en el sonido del grupo en comparación con otras bandas de la época.

Para 1978, el grupo lanza su segundo álbum titulado "Don't Look Back", el cual es de notable menor calidad que su antecesor y no deja muy satisfecho a Scholz, que acusa a la compañía discográfica de haberlo presionado para publicar este material; a pesar de esto, el disco alcanza ventas que le llevan al disco de platino y la canción que da título al disco se convierte en un éxito comercial. Tras ello, comienza un litigio legal entre la compañía y el grupo, que duró entre 1979 y 1981, el cual retrasó su tercer álbum durante 8 años (el cual iba a ser publicado originalmente en 1981). En el intertanto Tom Scholz líder de la banda expresó a los miembros del grupo que si deseaban realizar un proyecto musical alternativo ese era el momento pues el próximo proyecto de la banda tomaría un tiempo mayor. El guitarrista Barry Goudreau lanzó su proyecto solista titulado "Goudreau" en conjunto con otros músicos como banda de apoyo; entonces debido a un malentendido pues el sello discográfico de Barry Goudreau publicitó el disco con la consigna "music through science" (música a través de la ciencia), Tom Scholz expulsa a Barry Goudreau de la banda acusándolo de suplantar y plagiar en su proyecto musical personal la propuesta grupal de la banda cuestión que no era intención de Goudreau. El guitarrista Gary Phil sustituye a Goudreau y Fran Sheehan deja también al grupo. Scholz financia sus grabaciones vendiendo equipo, debido al asunto entre CBS y Boston. En 1982 el baterista Sib Hashian deja al grupo.

En 1986 se lanza, por fin, Third Stage y la canción "Amanda" llega inmediatamente a las listas de popularidad; esta canción es de un sonido muy distinto a las anteriores, una balada muy de los años ochenta, acertada por Scholz y la gran voz de Delp. El álbum alcanza disco de platino. Delp deja Boston en 1990 y es sustituido por Fran Cosmo.

El siguiente álbum de Boston no aparece hasta 1994; titulado Walk On, retoma ciertos sonidos de hard rock de los inicios del grupo. Los arreglos de la canción que titula al disco (dividida en tres segmentos) son considerados excesivos por algunos, pero la canción es una de las mejores piezas compuestas y arregladas por el ingenioso Scholz. Delp regresa al grupo ese mismo año.

En 1997 se publica el primer recopilatorio oficial de la banda que incluye algunos temas nuevos como "Tell me", "Higher Power", "The Star Spangled Banner/4th of July Reprise", así como una segunda versión más corta del "Higher Power", canción qué precisamente será elegida como sencillo para la presentación del disco.

El siguiente trabajo del grupo es Corporate America lanzado en 2002, ya con algunas tendencias pop y otras buenas canciones. Es de resaltar la participación de Fran Cosmo y su hijo Anthony, además de que entra Kimberley Dahme en el bajo y en algunos arreglos vocales. Jeff Neal (batería) completa la extensa alineación de este álbum.

Fran Cosmo y su hijo dejaron al grupo a principios de 2006 para formar su propia banda, dejando en ese momento a Brad Delp como única voz del grupo. Se especuló sobre una posible reunión con Barry Goudreau durante este periodo.

Uno de los aportes de Tom Scholz es la tecnología "Rockman", que fue utilizada por Def Leppard en su álbum Hysteria.

El 9 de marzo de 2007, una de las mejores voces en la historia del rock, Brad Delp, se suicidó inhalando monóxido de carbono. Fue hallado en su casa muerto en el baño con su cabeza encima de una almohada con una nota pegada en el cuello de su camisa con un clip que decía: "soy un alma solitaria". Pruebas de toxicología mostraron que se envenenó respirando monóxido de carbono y también hallaron otra nota en la puerta de su casa diciendo: "Cuando encuentren esta nota, ya estaré muerto, o si no, mi plan B es asfixiarme en mi coche".

El sustituto de Brad Delp fue nada menos que el cantante del grupo de rock cristiano Stryper, Michael Sweet, quien participó en el último tour de Boston.

Después de que Brad Delp nos dejara el pasado 9 de marzo de 2007, la banda tiene nuevo cantante, Tommy DeCarlo. El nuevo cantante, fue descubierto por casualidad por la mujer de Scholz cantando karaoke con una canción de Boston por Myspace. En el año 2013 Boston sacó a la luz un nuevo disco titulado "Live,Love & Hope", el día 3 diciembre sería la publicación en Estados Unidos, el día 6 en Europa y el 9 de diciembre en Reino Unido, así se publicitaba en la web oficial de la banda. En el disco se pudo escuchar la voz de Tommy de Carlo, David Victor, Kimberly Dahmne e incluso la de Scholz, líder de la banda, incluyendo además varias canciones con la voz de fallecido Brad Delp. La canción elegida como sencillo para la presentación del disco fue "Heaven on Earth",

Boston es considerado como un grupo de hard rock, combinando elementos del rock progresivo y heavy metal en su música. 
El excantante Brad Delp era bien conocido por su gran tesitura vocal y un timbre afinado y "cristalino" que se muestra en éxitos como "More Than a Feeling".

El guitarrista y compositor principal Tom Scholz abarca diversos estilos musicales, que van desde la música clásica hasta el pop inglés de 1960, que ha dado como resultado a un sonido único, se dio cuenta de forma más consistente en los dos primeros discos (Boston y Don't Look Back). Este sonido se caracteriza por provocar múltiples armonías combinadas con la guitarra, a menudo alternando sonidos y luego mezclando "capas" de guitarras eléctricas y acústicas. Scholz y Brian May son buenos ejemplos en 'perfectas' armonías de guitarra. Otro factor que contribuye es el uso de equipos de alta tecnología, en cuanto a efectos, amplificación electroacústica, etc. como los Rockman (creado por Tom Scholz), usado por guitarristas como de Journey Neal Schon, la banda ZZ Top, y Ted Nugent; pero por otra parte evitando usar "samplers", sintetizadores, computadores, midis, secuenciadores, y otros tipos de instrumentos en la creación de sonidos pues en palabras de Scholz tales elementos desnaturalizan la verdadera creación musical. 
El álbum Hysteria de Def Leppard fue creado usando tan sólo la tecnología de Rockman. "Combinando un sonido de guitarra profundo, agresivo, acortado en riffs y casi etéreo. 
Tiempo después pasó a un enfoque global más pesado, más bajo y oscuro (en los próximos dos álbumes) Third Stage y Walk On.

El cantante Brad Delp, que fue fuertemente influenciado por los Beatles, también era conocido por crear el sonido de Boston con su voz característica, que se vincula rápidamente con el grupo como a Freddie Mercury con Queen, Mick Jagger con los Rolling Stones, Jeff Lynne con Electric Light Orchestra, Steve Perry de Journey, Lou Gramm de Foreigner, Paul Rodgers de Bad Company, Roger Daltrey de The Who, Richard Sinclair con Hatfield & The North, Elliot Lurie con Looking Glass, Dennis DeYoung con Styx, Andy Fairweather-Low con Amen Corner, y Steve Walsh de Kansas.

xref.title: Departure from Canada (1966)
xref.body: After their final concerts in Toronto on August 17, 1966, The Beatles stayed overnight before flying out to Boston on August 18th. This departure marked their definitive farewell to Canadian stages, as they never toured again. "This time, they left forever."

xref.title: Mighty Mighty Bosstones – Formed 1983 Boston; Invented Skacore by Mixing Two-Tone with Hardcore; Major Label by 1993
xref.body: The Mighty Mighty Bosstones came together in 1983 when a group of guys became obsessed with the Two-Tone sound despite some members playing in hardcore bands influenced by Motorhead and AC/DC. This combination of Two-Tone ska with American hardcore became known as skacore — annoying to ska purists and initially baffling to hardcore kids, but eventually it clicked. By 1993 they had a major label record deal and a signature look involving plaid suits. "The Boss Tones took two-tone style Skah and made it with American hardcore to create something that was eventually called Skahcore."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: A Not-So Brief History of Ska: Part 2

xref.title: Operation Ivy (1987–1989) – Skacore Pioneers; Dissolved into Rancid
xref.body: Operation Ivy formed in 1987 and, like the Bosstones, embraced the blend of ska and hardcore known as skacore. They held it together for a couple of years and a couple of releases before dissolving and coalescing into a new band — Rancid, which became the first of the new wave of skacore bands to break out big. "Operation Ivy, they were formed in 1987 and like the muddy, muddy Boston's they were into that blend of Skah and Hardcore known as Skahcore."

xref.title: Boston Mosh Pit Lawsuit (1997)
xref.body: During Everclear's performance at The Paradise club in Boston on November 13, 1997, three members of the New England Patriots – quarterback Drew Bledsoe, backup quarterback Scott Zolak, and offensive lineman Max Lane (who weighed 305 pounds) – were in the mosh pit. Max Lane arced off the stage and landed on 23-year-old Tamika Messier, crushing her and causing severe neck, shoulder, and arm injuries, including two herniated discs and three fused vertebrae. Messier filed a $1.2 million lawsuit on December 10, 1997, against the club, Lane, Bledsoe, and Everclear, which was settled in March 1999, with Everclear contributing to the settlement and subsequently facing higher liability insurance premiums. "Everclear abandoned ended up with higher insurance premiums because of an NFL lineman."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Max Lane Stage Dive Incident (November 13, 1997)
xref.body: During an Everclear show at The Paradise in Boston, New England Patriots football players Drew Bledsoe, Scott Zolak, and Max Lane stage-dived. The 305-pound Max Lane landed on 23-year-old Tamika Messier, crushing her and causing severe neck, shoulder, and arm injuries, including herniated discs. "When he arced off the stage, he landed on 23-year-old Tamika Messier."

xref.title: Advocate for Canadian Music Scene
xref.body: Joshua Deu believed that Canada offered more opportunities for their band compared to Boston, citing a greater variety of music, richer culture, a more bohemian atmosphere, openness to new ideas, numerous arts festivals and galleries welcoming avant-garde performances, and readily available grants for musicians alongside affordable living. "Duh thought that Canada offered more opportunities for a band like theirs. You know, a greater variety of music, more culture, more pohemian, more open to new ideas, lots of arts festivals and art galleries that were welcoming to Algonne Guard musical performances."

xref.title: Airport and Airline Incidents
xref.body: Wes Scantlin has a notorious record of problematic behavior at airports and on airlines. On September 4, 2012, a dispute with a flight attendant over alcohol on an American Airlines flight from Boston to LA led to an emergency landing in Austin, Texas, where he was arrested. In early 2015, at Denver International Airport, he rode a baggage carousel into a restricted area. Later that same year, he was arrested for disorderly conduct at Milwaukee airport. In 2016, he was denied boarding a flight to Louisville, Kentucky, due to extreme intoxication. In 2017, he was arrested at LAX for attempting to board a flight with a BB gun and has since been banned from the airport unless traveling for work. "West has a thing for getting in trouble with airlines and airports."

xref.body: Joshua Deu formed an early version of Arcade Fire with Win Butler, having been a fellow student from their school in Boston. "When had formed with Joshua Duh, a fellow student from the school in Boston?"

xref.title: Band Origins and Early Gigs
xref.body: The band was formed in Massachusetts in 1996. Their initial performances took place in the basement of a barber shop. They significantly developed their sound and presence after touring with The Mighty Mighty Bosstones, another band from the Boston area. "Their first gigs were in the basement of a barber shop, but after the muddy, muddy boss tones, another Boston area band, took them on tour, they really came into their own."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Berkeley College of Music Education
xref.body: Furthered his musical education by studying bass at the prestigious Berkeley in Boston. "You went to Berkeley, right? Yeah, eventually. Berkeley, Aboston, yeah, to study bass."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Berklee College of Music Admission
xref.body: Ian Thornley was admitted to the Berklee School of Music in Boston after submitting a 4-track demo featuring his compositions and various instrumental parts. His prior musical training, including piano studies with jazz musician Darwin Grosse, contributed to his foundational understanding of harmony and theory, which likely aided his admission. "I just, I had put together, you know, I had a little foretrack thing and I had written a bunch of compositions and, and don't know all these parts, put them all together and just sent those down."

xref.title: Boston Origin and Cabaret Sound
xref.body: This two-piece group from Boston has a unique sound and look, described as if Siouxsie and the Banshees were performing in East Berlin cabarets in 1932. "There are two piece groups out of Boston and they look and sound like what might have happened had Suzy and the Banshee's been playing the Cabaret's and East Berlin in 1932."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Boston Prep School Exposure
xref.body: Both Win and his younger brother, William Butler, attended prep school in Boston, where they were exposed to influential bands like Joy Division, New Order, James, The Cure, Echo and the Bunnymen, and The Smiths, shaping their early musical tastes. "And this is where they were exposed to music from. Joy Division, New Order, James the Cure, Echo and the Bunnieman and the Smiths."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Who the Hell is Arcade Fire? Part 1

xref.title: Boston-Based 20-Somethings
xref.body: The group is based in Boston and is composed of musicians in their twenties who have developed a significant obsession with a specific type of sound from the 1980s. "Passion Pit is a Boston-based group of 20-somethings who, even though they weren't even born until halfway through the decade, have developed a major obsession with a certain type of sound from the 1980s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Roots of New Wave through Techno-Pop

xref.title: Contrarian Persona
xref.body: Jonathan Richman, a Boston native, presented himself as the antithesis of the prevailing big names of his era. He kept his hair short, actively opposed drug use, and was frequently heard yelling "I hate hippies" around Boston. Unlike many contemporaries who favored The Beatles, The Rolling Stones, or the growing prog rock scene, Richman preferred the raw, unconventional sound of The Velvet Underground and The Stooges, leading him to be perceived as "weird" by mainstream audiences. "Jonathan Richmond was the complete opposite of the big names of the day. He wore his hair short and he was against using drugs. He could often be heard yelling, I hate hippies around Boston."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Deep Hockey Connections
xref.body: The band has a profound love for hockey, with connections running deeper than common knowledge. Gord Downie's godfather is Harry Sinden, the legendary Boston Bruins coach and general manager. Downie wore a Bruins sweater in the "Courage" video, and songs like "50 Mission Cap," "Fireworks," "Lonely End of the Rink," and "Heaven is a Better Place Today" all include hockey themes or references. "To know the tragically hip is to know that they're huge hockey fans. And that love for hockey runs a lot deeper than most people know. ... Hockey literally runs in the blood of the tragically hip. Well in the veins of Gord Downey anyway."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Career and Persona
xref.body: Susan Dietrich, known as The Space Lady, is from Pueblo, Colorado. For many years, she was a street musician, frequently performing in cities like Boston and San Francisco. She was easily recognizable by her unique outfit: a silver plastic helmet adorned with white wings and a flashing light. She initially played the accordion. "She wore a silver plastic helmet adorned with white wings and a flashing light on top. And she played the accordion."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Fan Headbanging Observation
xref.body: During their North American tour between January 22 and January 25, 1969, Led Zeppelin played at the Boston Tea Party, where fans in the front row were observed banging their heads on the stage in time with the music. A year later, during a performance in London, the front row again engaged in collective headbanging. "The band played a venue called the Boston Tea Party and fans down front were seen banging their heads on the stage in time with the music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Life and Education
xref.body: William Butler, Win Butler's younger brother by two years, shared the same upbringing, moving with his family to The Woodlands near Houston in 1984. He attended prep school in Boston alongside his brother, where he was exposed to influential post-punk and alternative bands. "William Butler, Wins younger brother by two years, had the same upbringing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Who the Hell is Arcade Fire? Part 1

xref.title: Family and Hockey Influence
xref.body: Gord's godfather was Harry Sinden, a family friend who later became the coach of Team Canada in the 1972 Canada-Russia series and subsequently worked as coach and general manager for the Boston Bruins. This connection influenced Gord's childhood passion for the Bruins, leading him to wear number four like Bobby Orr, before switching to play goal, a position he thoroughly enjoyed. "His godfather was Harry Sinden, a friend of the family. Harry would later go on to be the coach of Team Canada and the 72 Canada Russia series and then work as coach in GM with the Boston Bruins. And this is why as a kid, Gord was such a Bruins fan."

The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formation in Boston
xref.body: Big Wreck was formed in Boston, Massachusetts, out of collaborations between Ian Thornley, Brian Doherty, Dave Henning, and Forest Williams, who had met while attending Berklee School of Music. "It was formed in Boston."

xref.title: Harry Sinden as Godfather
xref.body: Gord Downie's godfather was Harry Sinden, who was the coach and general manager of the Boston Bruins, reflecting Gord's lifelong passion for hockey. "Knowing that Gord was brought into this world with Bruin's coach and GM Harry Sinden as his godfather, and that he was a lifelong hockey fan and player."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Hockey Bloodline (Harry Sinden)
xref.body: Gord Downie's deep connection to hockey is highlighted by his godfather, Harry Sinden, who is the legendary coach, general manager, and president of the Boston Bruins, as well as the coach for the Canadian team in the 1972 Canada-Russia Series. This family tie is reflected in Downie wearing a Boston Bruins sweater in the "Courage" music video. "Hockey literally runs in the blood of the tragically hip. Well in the veins of Gord Downey anyway. ... That's because his godfather is Harry Sinden, the legendary coach, general manager and president of the Bruins. He was also the coach for the Canadian team in the 72 Canada Rushes series."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Hockey Goalie and Harry Sinden Connection
xref.body: Downie was a goalie for Amherst View hockey teams that were good enough to win a provincial title one year. His godfather was Harry Sinden, a Stanley Cup-winning coach for the Boston Bruins and head coach for Team Canada in the 1972 series with the Soviets. This connection, stemming from Sinden's real estate partnership with Downie's father, Edgar, explains why Gord wore number four (Bobby Orr's number) when he played hockey and provided background for The Tragically Hip's song "Fireworks." "His godfather was Harry Sinden, a Stanley Cup winning coach for the Boston Bruins, which explains why Gord wore number four, Bobby Horace's number when he played hockey."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Kurt Cobain's Plagiarism Concerns
xref.body: While writing "Nevermind," Kurt Cobain was frequently troubled by the thought that he might be inadvertently plagiarizing other artists. He worried about similarities between "Smells Like Teen Spirit" and Boston's "More Than a Feeling," as well as the quiet/loud structure resembling The Pixies' style. He also considered how Jazz Coleman might react to "Come As You Are." "Yet as he was writing it, Kurt Cobain was nagged by the thought that he just might be ripping off other people."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Limited Musical Knowledge Focused on Hardcore
xref.body: Nate Mendel admits to having the "least depth of musical knowledge" among his bandmates, primarily caring about hardcore music for a formative period of about ten years. He often relies on Taylor Hawkins to introduce him to other bands, such as Boston. "I only cared about hardcore for about 10 years. Like those formative 10 years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Nuggets Band from Boston
xref.body: Formed in 1962, The Standells were a "Nuggets band" known for their classic 60s Garage Rock sound. Their song "Dirty Water" was specifically written about the heavily polluted Charles River in Boston. "The stand-ells were formed in 1962 and recorded this song written about the heavily polluted Charles River in Boston."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 4: Garage Rock

xref.title: Post-Breakup Success of Members
xref.body: Following the band's dissolution in 1974, two of its members went on to achieve greater success. Drummer David Robertson found work with another Boston group, The Cars. Keyboardist Jerry Harrison joined the new band The Talking Heads. Both The Cars and The Talking Heads would later become significant components of the American New Wave era. "However, two members of the band went on to bigger and better things. Drummer David Robertson found work with another Boston group called The Cars and Keyboard is Jerry Harrison soon hooked up with a new band called The Talking Heads."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rejection of Straight Edge Philosophy
xref.body: Unlike some Boston hardcore bands influenced by Ian MacKaye's straight edge philosophy, Gang Green was an example of a group that embraced drugs and alcohol. They were known for their fierce approach, in contrast to the "Boston Crew" who policed shows. "Other groups kind of liked their drugs and alcohol. And that included the very fierce gang green."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rockman Inventor
xref.body: A graduate of MIT and leader of the band Boston, Tom Scholz invented the Rockman. This innovative small box device provided players with the fuzz, distortion, and sustain typically associated with a large, loud amplifier, but in a compact format that allowed for quiet enjoyment and practice. "Tom Schoetz, the leader of Boston and a graduate of MIT, invented something called the rock man, which gave the player all the fuss and distortion and sustain of a Big Am playing loud, but in a small box that could be enjoyed quietly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Distortion and Feedback

xref.title: Roxbury Living Experience
xref.body: While attending Berklee, Ian moved into the old Tremont Towers in Roxbury, Boston, with Brian Doherty and Dave Henning. This was an eye-opening and "scary" experience for a kid from Toronto, as they were living in a rough neighborhood. He quickly learned to "shut up, keep my head down and get where I was going, especially if it was dark." "it was scary is what it was. It was scary."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Ian Thornley - In His Own Words: Part 1

xref.title: Sebadoh Lo-Fi Project (Early 1990s)
xref.body: While working with Jay Mascus in the band Dinosaurs Jr. in the Boston area, Lou Barlow maintained a separate low-fi project that he eventually named Sebadoh. This project exclusively released music on Shrimper, a cassette-only label, further cementing Barlow's dedication to the raw, unpolished, and accessible nature of cassette-based lo-fi recording and distribution. "When he wasn't working with them, Lou had his own low-fi project he eventually called Cebado, which released music on a cassette-only label called Shrimper."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Stage Diving Injury Lawsuit
xref.body: On November 13, 1997, during an Everclear show at The Paradise in Boston, stage diving was prevalent. Two New England Patriots players, Drew Bledsoe and Scott Zolak, along with lineman Max Lane (who weighed 305 pounds), climbed onto the stage. Lane dove into the crowd, landing on 23-year-old Tamika Messier and crushing her. She suffered neck, shoulder, and arm injuries, including two herniated discs and three fused vertebrae. Messier filed a lawsuit on December 10 against the players, their club, and the band, eventually receiving $1.2 million for her pain and suffering. "Lane Dove. He landed on 23 year old Tamika Messier crushing her. She suffered injuries to her neck, shoulders and arms."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Third Wave Pioneers
xref.body: Formed in 1983 in Boston, The Mighty Mighty Bosstones were early practitioners of the third wave of Ska, initially inspired by the Two Tone movement but also incorporating hard rock influences from bands like ACDC, Motorhead, and Social Distortion. They became prominent in the late 1980s and early 1990s by fusing Ska with hardcore elements. "The Mighty Mighty Boss Tones. They were formed in 1983 and inspired by the whole two-tone thing, at least originally."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: University Studies
xref.body: After prep school in Boston, William Butler pursued higher education at Northwestern University in Chicago, where he majored in poetry and Slavic studies. "From there, William went to Northwestern University in Chicago where he majored in poetry and Slavic studies."
